notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Demo Gateway G400 versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 are affected by a fictional exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor issue. Version 1.2.0 contains the simulated fix; the separate 2.0.0 branch is not affected.

notes.title: Technical overview
notes.text: The fictional status endpoint exposes configuration information without an authorization check. An unauthorized user may read configuration data in this simulated scenario. The issue is intentionally described without executable attack instructions or payloads.

notes.title: General recommendations
notes.text: For this demonstration, inventory the deployed version, restrict management access, back up configuration, and schedule the update to 1.2.0. Validate normal operation after updating. Disable public status access and restrict the endpoint to authorized administration hosts.

notes.title: Are these real vulnerabilities?
notes.text: No. All products, issue identifiers, release versions, impact statements, and scores are synthetic. No real CVE identifiers are assigned. The example.com references illustrate the document structure and are not working support or download endpoints.

notes.title: Test data disclaimer
notes.text: This document is provided solely for testing CSAF processing and human-readable display. Do not treat it as evidence that any real product is vulnerable or use it as operational security guidance.

notes.title: Scope and prerequisites
notes.text: The affected service must be reachable over the network; no account is required in this synthetic scenario. Only versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 are covered by the affected status. The 2.0.0 branch uses a different implementation and is not affected.

remediations.details: In this fictional scenario, update Demo Gateway G400 from 1.0.0 or 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 during a maintenance window. Back up configuration, verify the installed version after the update, and confirm normal operation. The linked URL is a placeholder, not a download service.

restart_required.details: A simulated device or application restart is required after the update.

remediations.details: Disable public status access and restrict the endpoint to authorized administration hosts. This reduces exposure but does not replace the fictional software fix.
Restrict service access to trusted networks, monitor unexpected service activity, and review administrative access until the simulated update is complete.
